page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 CPU architecture. It features 20 vCPUs with a shared allocation model, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.8 GB of RAM per core. The primary compute accelerators are two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. A key architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation model, which may introduce performance variability under sustained, non-GPU-bound CPU workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a high density of system memory and modern GPU acceleration relative to its CPU core count. This makes it suitable for workloads that offload heavy computations to the GPUs rather than relying on dedicated CPU cores. Appropriate workloads include machine learning inference, video transcoding, graphics rendering, and data science tasks that benefit from dual NVIDIA L4 accelerators and a large 256.0 GB memory footprint.
